full_judgment: The aforesaid observation was made in connection with a review petition which arose out of a judgment and decree passed by the High Court in First Appeal No. 68 of 1954, D/-4-5-1960. The said judgment out of which the review petition arose was from a decree passed by the trial court in a money suit. An appeal from such decree lay to the District Court under section 21 of the Rajasthan Civil Courts Ordinance, 1950. The aforesaid observation is an answer to the contention and lays down the principle of law with regard to the power of the High Court under section 24 of the Code so far as it relates to withdrawal and transfer of an appeal or other proceeding to any Court subordinate to it or to itself. We do not also find in the language of Section 24(1) (b) of the Code that the power of withdrawal of any suit, appeal and other proceeding pending in any court subordinate to the High Court Division to itself is so circumscribed by the right of appeal or revision to the Court subordinate to the High Court Division. The power conferred under section 24(J)(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure is an unfettered one as and loss of a valuable right of revision or appeal as contended by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties is no bar to the exercise of such power by the High Court Division.
